key_provisions_or_claims: Existing personal care robot safety standards call for child safety but give no specific methods.
Authors built a correspondence table mapping JIS B 8445, B 8446, B 9700, Z 8050 and ST toy standards to risk assessment steps.
Gaps: standards do not address children actively contacting self-moving robots; sound warnings may not be understood by children.
Proposes caregiver-oriented residual risk information and operation-prevention measures like hold-to-run buttons.
Low-speed load-cell collision experiments show cushioning materials reduce impact force but may increase impulse.
annotation.summary_en: Japanese conference paper on safety design of personal care robots with regard to children. It maps Japanese safety standards (JIS B 8445, Z 8050, ST toy standards) onto risk assessment steps, identifies gaps for children's active contact, and reports basic low-speed collision experiments with cushioning materials using a load cell.
